issues.description: Method-naming inconsistency for the farm song: the problem statement (UML and task text) instructs students to implement printFarmSong(), whereas both the template and the provided solution define and use singFarmSong(). This discrepancy can confuse students about which method name/signature to implement and may lead to mismatches with tests or instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement to instruct implementation of singFarmSong(), or rename the template/solution methods to printFarmSong(). Ensure the chosen name appears identically in the UML, task description, template stubs, and solution so students implement the correct method signature.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to a method named printFarmSong() (UML and task description), but both the template and the solution use the method name singFarmSong() in Farm.java. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (printing/singing the farm song) can confuse students when mapping the requirements to the provided code and when implementing or invoking the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() everywhere (preferred if template/solution/testing expect that name), or rename the method in template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() so it matches the problem description. Ensure tests and examples use the same identifier.
